news.title: China demands answers after man dies in ICE custody
news.text:
The Chinese government has asked the United States to investigate the death of a 51-year-old Chinese national who died hours after being booked into an Immigration and Customs Enforcement facility in the U.S. territory of Saipan, according to news reports.

Lianyong Wei, who had been arrested on several charges after being accused of assaulting a family of five at their residence, died Aug. 23, ICE officials said.

"We have expressed serious concerns to the relevant U.S. authorities over this incident and required a timely and thorough investigation into the cause of Mr. Wei's death, notification of the findings, measures to prevent any recurrence of similar incidents, and assistance to the family of the deceased in handling the aftermath," PBS reported the consulate as saying in a statement.

Wei was first arrested on Aug. 21 by officers of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands Department of Safety. Saipan is the capital and largest of the Northern Mariana Islands, part of the Pacific’s Mariana Archipelago just north of Guam.

U.S. forces claimed the islands of Saipan and Tinian from Japan during World War II in 1944, and the Northern Mariana Islands officially became a U.S. commonwealth and territory in the 1970s and 1980s, according to the U.S. Department of the Interior.

The islands are among several American territories in which ICE has detention facilities, according to the Transactional Records Access Clearinghouse, a public research project at Syracuse University in New York that tracks immigration enforcement.

"While many of these detention facilities are concentrated along the southwest border with Mexico, every state and territory—including Puerto Rico, Guam, the Virgin Islands, and the Northern Mariana Islands—has at least one ICE detention facility," the group said. "Some detention facilities are temporary holding rooms, while others are designed for long-term stays. Some hold only a single person on one occasion during the entire year, while others have tens of thousands who pass through their doors during this same period."

ICE also has a facility at the U.S. naval base in Guantanamo Bay, Cuba.

After his arrest, Wei was charged with assault with a dangerous weapon, disturbing the peace and aggravated assault and battery, ICE said in a news release. With removal proceedings already underway, he was placed in the agency's custody on Aug. 22.

A corrections officer conducting routine checks found Wei unresponsive about 7 a.m. the next morning, ICE said. He was immediately taken to the Commonwealth Health Care Corporation Emergency Room, where medical staff tried to revive him without success.

He was pronounced dead about 7:30 a.m. Chamorro Standard Time, the agency said. Cause of death is still under investigation.

Wei had been paroled by U.S. Customs and Border Protection in February 2019, with temporary authorization to remain in Saipan for a week, the agency said. However, ICE said he remained beyond that date without permission from the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.

U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services issued Wei a notice to appear on July 14, 2026. His next hearing had been scheduled for this month.

"Following this incident, the Department is reviewing relevant procedures and will implement any necessary corrective actions to strengthen prevention and response measures," said Anthony Torres, commissioner of the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands Department of Corrections, in a statement obtained by PBS.

Wei is the 57th immigrant detainee to die in ICE custody since President Donald Trump took office and the 24th such death in 2026, according to the agency's detainee death reporting list.

The tally doesn’t include people released from ICE custody while they were ill who died soon afterward.

For instance, according to northjersey.com, part of the USA Today Network, Prisciliano Trejo Ricano, 29, reported coughing up blood, migraines, severe pain and increasing weakness while detained for several weeks in Georgia before being diagnosed with aggressive leukemia. ICE released him while he was unconscious in a hospital and he died eight days later.

A few days later, Jose Chajon-Raxon of Guatemala died at a hospital in Newark, New Jersey, after ICE granted him a “discretionary release.” He had experienced seizure-like symptoms and was hospitalized while in custody.

Neither is included in the list of immigrant detainee deaths. ICE stopped reporting deaths occurring within 30 days of a person’s release from its custody in June, meaning they aren’t subject to previous levels of reporting, internal oversight or Congressional notification.

Advocates and some lawmakers say the change will hamper efforts to determine whether insufficient care in ICE facilities contributed to such deaths.
news.author: Usa Today

news.title: Trump names Adam Telle acting secretary of the Army following Dan Driscoll's resignation
news.text: President Donald Trump on Thursday announced he was appointing Adam Telle, assistant secretary of the Army for Civil Works, as acting secretary of the Army. "I am pleased to announce that Adam Telle, the current Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works, will become Acting Secretary of the Army, effective immediately," Trump posted on Truth Social. "He is a Great Patriot, who is respected by all." He made the announcement after Army Secretary Dan Driscoll submitted his resignation to the president earlier this week. ARMY SECRETARY DAN DRISCOLL SUBMITS RESIGNATION TO TRUMP Telle, who was nominated by Trump and confirmed by the Senate in 2025, oversees the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' Civil Works program, where his responsibilities include flood and storm protection, commercial waterways and Clean Water Act permitting. Previously, Telle served as chief of staff to Sen. Bill Hagerty, R-Tenn., and was Trump's chief liaison to the Senate during the president's first administration, when he led the White House Office of Legislative Affairs' Senate team. Before that, Telle served on the Senate Appropriations Committee subcommittee responsible for overseeing the Department of Homeland Security's budget. He also spent 10 years in the office of former Sen. Thad Cochran, R-Miss., where he served as deputy chief of staff, legislative director and the senator's top national security staffer. TRUMP’S ARMY SECRETARY HUNT TAKES SHAPE AS INSIDERS FLOAT POTENTIAL PICKS Telle is viewed as having strong relationships with senators on Capitol Hill, which could prove important as the administration works to confirm Army nominees stalled in the Senate. The appointment fills a key leadership vacancy atop the nation's largest military branch. Driscoll's exit came after he reportedly butted heads with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth over the Army's transformation and readiness, including Driscoll's belief that Hegseth had hindered those efforts, Fox News Digital previously reported. US ARMY OFFERING DEFENSE FIRMS 'CONCIERGE ACCESS' TO TEST WEAPONS AT MILITARY RANGES The outgoing Army secretary said Wednesday would be his "last full day" in the position, adding that serving under Trump and Hegseth had been "the honor of a lifetime." "I had the privilege of working with them to modernize and accelerate how the Army mans, trains, and equips the most lethal fighting force on the face of the earth," Driscoll said in a statement posted on X. "We could not have made the progress we did without the support of Secretary Hegseth," he continued. "I am forever grateful to President Trump for the opportunity to once again serve my country." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital's Ashley J. DiMella and Fox News' Jennifer Griffin contributed to this report.
news.summary: Adam Telle steps in as acting Army secretary after Dan Driscoll's resignation amid reported clashes with Pete Hegseth over Army readiness efforts.
news.author: Michael Sinkewicz

news.title: Trump’s White House releases deportation video games
news.text:
Rights groups criticised the online games as the Trump administration stepped up its mass arrest and deportation programme for undocumented migrants. (White House pic)
WASHINGTON: US president Donald Trump's White House on Thursday unveiled a website featuring classic arcade games - but with a "MAGA" twist, in which players can deport migrants and build a border wall.
Rights groups swiftly criticised the release of the online games, which comes as the Trump administration steps up its mass arrest and deportation programme for undocumented migrants.
One game called Rio Run - an updated version of the game Snake - features a digital version of US border czar Tom Homan chasing migrants with different skin colors next to the Rio Grande river on the Mexican border.
Another game based on the block-stacking game Tetris is called Build the Wall. "Protect the border from the coming horde," the instructions say.
A third involves collecting nets to put in so-called "Trump accounts" - investment accounts containing a US$1,000 deposit for children born in 2025 through 2028.
The White House account on X posted a video with the "Make America Great Again" logo MAGA, based on the logo of video game maker Sega.
"CAN'T STOP WINNING. Build the wall. Deport. Fill a Trump Account," it says.
"This administration is laser focused on ways to innovate and tell the story of the President's many accomplishments in a way that resonates with every American," the White House said in a statement to AFP.
"This is an effort to further contrast between a culture of fun and winning and the dark socialist vision Democrats have for America."
Rights groups criticised the White House for the gaming website.
"Makes me sick. They've been playing games with people's lives for years, now they've made a video game of what they're doing," Amerika Garcia Grewal, co-director of the Frontera Federation in Eagle Pass, Texas, told AFP.
The game designers "have lost touch with what it means to be human and care for others."
Adriana Jasso, program coordinator for AMIGOS San Diego Community, who works at the border, said the arcade-style games showed a fundamental "lack of seriousness" from the administration.
"The cruelty, the extremity of the administration... is no longer surprising," she said.
The White House seems intent on dehumanising and ridiculing migrants, even as people die in detention centres, she said.
"This presents the issue as if it were a game, when in fact it is not."
Trump campaigned on a promise to expel millions of undocumented migrants and has taken several actions since returning to power aimed at speeding up deportations and reducing border crossings.
His White House meanwhile has long used social media stunts to ram home its points and troll liberal opponents, and has sparked a backlash from several artists by using their music without permission.
news.summary: The White House unveils classic arcade games with a 'MAGA' twist, allowing players to deport migrants and build a border wall.
news.author: AFP

news.title: DR Congo latest to promise moving Israel embassy to Jerusalem
news.text:
Israel captured the eastern part of Jerusalem from Jordan in the 1967 Six-Day War and annexed it, declaring Jerusalem to be its eternal, undivided capital. (EPA Images pic)
JERUSALEM: The Democratic Republic of Congo said Thursday it would move its embassy in Israel to Jerusalem, joining a small group of countries including the US in taking the symbolic step of backing Israeli sovereignty in the contested holy city.
After a visit by president Felix-Antoine Tshisekedi, the two countries in a statement said they would take steps for "the relocation of the embassy of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from Tel Aviv to Jerusalem", without giving a timeline.
Tshisekedi and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in a meeting spoke of their "shared commitment to strengthening diplomatic relations", the statement said.
Tshisekedi has spoken warmly about Israel for years, saying his support is driven by his Christian faith. He has also been eager for support from the US, which has increasingly pressured Rwanda over armed rebel advances in DR Congo.
The announcement comes weeks after Colombia's new hard-right president, Abelardo de la Espriella, also announced that he would move his country's embassy to Jerusalem, a sharp shift from his leftist predecessor who criticised Israel over its Gaza offensive.
The vast majority of countries, if they recognise Israel, keep their embassies in Tel Aviv on the grounds that the status of Jerusalem will be settled in a final resolution of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
President Donald Trump shattered that consensus in 2018 during his first term by moving the US embassy to Jerusalem, which is home to Israel's parliament, prime minister and most other major governmental institutions.
Since Trump's move, only a handful of small, US-aligned countries have followed suit - Fiji, Guatemala, Honduras, Papua New Guinea and Paraguay.
Kosovo and Somaliland, which are not member-states of the United Nations, have also opened what they consider their embassies in Jerusalem.
Argentine President Javier Milei, another right-wing Latin American who is an outspoken supporter of Israel, has promised to move his country's embassy to Jerusalem.
The shift has not yet taken place, however, reportedly due to disagreement over an Israeli company's plans to drill in the British-ruled Falkland Islands, which Argentina claims and calls the Malvinas.
Israel captured the eastern part of Jerusalem from Jordan in the 1967 Six-Day War and annexed it, declaring Jerusalem, home to Judaism's holiest site, to be its eternal, undivided capital.
news.summary: President Felix-Antoine Tshisekedi has spoken warmly about Israel for years, saying his support is driven by his Christian faith.
news.author: AFP

news.title: Tucker Carlson Says Greg Abbott About to Lose in Texas: What Polls Show
news.text: Tucker Carlson is warning that Texas Governor Greg Abbott could be in serious political trouble heading into the 2026 midterm elections, as Democrat Gina Hinojosa has narrowed the gap in the traditionally Republican state. The latest polling shows a close race, giving Hinojosa an opening as she seeks to unseat the three-term Republican governor. The contest comes as Abbott faces criticism over his shifting position on artificial intelligence data centers. Abbott previously promoted Texas as an AI hub but has recently moved toward greater oversight of the industry. On August 3, he directed the Public Utility Commission of Texas and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas to conduct a comprehensive audit of data centers seeking to connect to the state’s power grid, requiring the audit to be completed before projects could move forward. Abbott said projects that fail to meet state requirements will be denied connections, citing concerns about the strain data centers could place on Texas’ electricity grid. Hinojosa has made the data-center controversy a part of her campaign, arguing that Abbott is reversing course to protect his reelection chances and because voters have grown increasingly concerned about the projects. In an email to Newsweek on Thursday, Texas Democratic Party spokesman Jacob Long accused Abbott of previously giving data centers generous tax breaks and promoting Texas as an “AI playground for billionaires,” before declaring that voters would send him into retirement and elect Hinojosa. The criticism comes as opposition to data centers has spread across party lines, with a recent Texas Politics Project poll finding only 30 percent supported having a data center in their community. Newsweek reached out to Abbott's campaign via online form on Thursday for comment. What To Know In an episode of The Tucker Carlson Show released Wednesday, Carlson sat down with podcast host Saagar Enjeti. Enjeti said that Donald Trump has run numerous times now on rebuilding America but, as of late, has backed AI and data centers. "How about a bill in Congress that Trump could call for, saying, 'You want your data centers, okay, but we're not gonna turn this into East Germany," Carlson said. "If we had abundant cheap power, none of this would really be as much of a conversation, but it is actually living in a world where the administration is coming to the back of these data center companies and is in many cases is attacking Republican governors who, again, in my opinion, are just trying to do some very sensible stuff," Enjeti later added. "Greg Abbott, who, let's not pretend he's doing this out of the goodness of his own heart, he dragged kicking and screaming to the data center moratorium." "He's about to lose that election," Carlson said. "He very well may," Enjeti said. "But he signed the data center moratorium, and in it, all he says is, 'Look, we're doing a moratorium; we have to figure out rural land use and water, noise generation, we need to make sure that you don't get certain tax breaks. We just need to make things normal so that when the local community allows the data center to be built, that they reap some of the benefits. And Trump comes out and is like, I think it's a mistake." Hinojosa reacted to the remark on X on Thursday, saying, "You heard it from Tucker Carlson: Greg Abbott is going to lose." Meanwhile, on Monday, Trump took to Truth Social arguing that communities that reject data centers risk falling behind economically, saying the projects can bring jobs and lower taxes. "The good news is that there are plenty of other places that want them. If we kill the Golden Goose, you will only have yourselves to blame. China could not be happier with this anti Data Center movement. Actually, they can’t believe it is happening!" Trump said. Data centers are also emerging as a growing political sticking point within the Republican Party, putting Trump at odds with members of his own party who are increasingly concerned about voter backlash. While speaking during the White House press briefing on Thursday, Vice President JD Vance said, “A very large chunk of it, not all of it, of course, but a very large chunk of it, is that people associate data centers with ‘my neighborhood's going to get worse.’ In particular, ‘my power bills are going to go up.'" “The way to bridge that gap,” Vance said, is to help put power back into the grid. Vance was also asked about Carlson during the briefing, specifically on remarks he made against Republican nominee for Michigan Senate, Mike Rogers. "Tucker is a friend of mine," Vance said. "I'm not gonna play the game where I throw friends under the bus because I have political disagreements with them." What Polls Show A poll by Overton Insights and the Texas Public Policy Foundation found Abbott leading Hinojosa 47 percent to 46 percent among likely voters. The poll of 1,167 likely voters was conducted August 24-26 and had a margin of error of 2.9 percent. University of Texas/Texas Politics Project poll shows Abbott up with 45 percent over Hinojosa's 40 percent. The poll surveyed 1,200 registered voters in Texas from August 5-13, 2026, and had a margin of error of 2.83 percent. An Emerson College Polling/Nexstar Media survey shows that Abbott is up with 49 percent compared to Hinojosa's 45 percent. The poll was taken from August 9-10, 2026, among 1,000 likely Texas voters, with a margin of error of 3 percent. The polling, however, does not yet show Abbott losing. The overall trend has pointed somewhat toward a more competitive race, and Hinojosa's standing could make the governor's race one of the more closely watched contests in Texas this November. Meanwhile, midterm elections are commonly seen as a measure of public approval for the current president, and the president's party has traditionally lost seats during them. Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Jason Lemon and Gray R. Thomas
news.summary: The tightening contest comes as Abbott faces criticism over his shifting position on artificial intelligence data centers.
news.author: Anna Commander

news.title: Trump says US will soon prevail over Iran
news.text:

news.title: What we know about Maria Bartiromo's abrupt exit from Fox News
news.text:
Maria Bartiromo's abrupt departure from Fox News Media is raising questions about what led to the shocking move.

Fox News Media announced they were cutting ties with the prominent anchor effective immediately in a Sept. 3 press release. Bartiromo, who was with the network for over a decade, had not appeared on any of her three shows since Aug. 9.

"We thank Maria for her work over the last 12 ½ years and wish her all the best on her next chapter," the brief statement said, offering no further explanation.

Here is what we know about her departure:

Who is taking over Maria Bartiromo's role?

The press release stated the final episode of Bartiromo's three-hour weekday show "Mornings with Maria" had aired that morning on Fox Business Network and would be renamed "Mornings with FOX Business" beginning Sept. 4, and would be hosted by rotating anchors.

Additionally, the release said the weekly program "Maria Bartiromo’s Wall Street" was shifting to "FBN’s Wall Street" with rotating anchors, and former Republican congressman Jason Chaffetz would be stepping in to host Fox News Channel’s "Sunday Morning Futures" until a new host was found.

Fox Business also revealed plans to introduce a new weekday programming schedule in coming weeks.

Why did Maria Bartiromo leave Fox?

Bartiromo joined Fox Business to cover Wall Street in 2014 after two decades at CNBC. She became known for being the first woman to report from the floor of the New York Stock Exchange and for her staunch support of the Trump administration.

While President Donald Trump and his associates have praised Bartiromo, with Trump even appointing her to the board of the Kennedy Center last year, she has been engulfed in legal trouble for Fox in recent years.

In 2021, voting machine company Dominion Voting launched a $1.6 billion defamation lawsuit against Fox News, naming Bartiromo as one of the anchors who spread “stolen election” falsehoods about the 2020 presidential election. The matter was later settled for $787.5 million.

Shortly after the settlement in 2023, top-rated Fox News anchor Tucker Carlson separated from the network. He had been hired in 2016 to replace Bill O’Reilly, who was fired after settling a sexual harassment investigation.

Bartiromo's exit comes amid the White House's search for a new press secretary, leading to speculation that may be her next role. However, Vice President JD Vance dismissed the idea at a Sept. 3 press briefing.

“I don’t know, man,” Vance said, laughing at a question about whether Bartiromo is going to be the next press secretary. “No, I don’t think so.”

Maria Bartiromo's exit follows Fox's apology for comments on her show

In June, Fox News issued an apology that Bartiromo had to read on air addressing comments made by entrepreneur Kevin O'Leary, who said the Chinese government was funding opponents of his Utah data center during an appearance on Bartiromo's program.

Fox News and the "Shark Tank" investor are now facing a defamation lawsuit from two Utah nonprofits and their founders over the comments.
news.author: Usa Today

news.title: Iran threatens 'powerful response' as Israel downplays risk of escalation over holidays
news.text: Defense Minister Israel Katz said Iran “likes to attack on Jewish holidays,” while Tehran warned that a full-scale Israeli attack on the Ali al-Taher ridge would be met with a “powerful response.” But despite those warnings, threats and reports suggesting the possibility of an escalation with Iran, senior Israeli officials stressed that they had heard of no Iranian intention to act against Israel in the near term. Reuters reported Thursday that Iran had sent a message to the United States last month warning that any “full-scale Israeli attack” on the strategic ridge in Lebanon, where Iranian military personnel were said to be positioned alongside Hezbollah terrorists, would draw an Iranian response. On Thursday night, the IDF said it had established operational control over the ridge, completed clearing it and was preparing to neutralize the site, adding that “some of the terrorists were eliminated and some fled.” The message from Tehran reflects Iran’s direct and continuing involvement in southern Lebanon and its ties to Hezbollah. However, neither the IDF statement announcing the completion of operations to clear underground infrastructure at Ali al-Taher nor a video released by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu mentioned Iranian personnel. A senior Israeli official said U.S. President Donald Trump had been raising the tone surrounding the possibility of escalation, but that the concern remained largely general. Still, several developments in recent days have created a sense that “something is happening.” On Wednesday, Katz told ynet and Yedioth Ahronoth’s “Decision Time: Democracy and Society” conference that “as U.S. pressure on Iran increases, and as the friction and economic pressure on Iran increase, there is a greater likelihood they will attack. They like to attack on Jewish holidays because they hate Jews.” On Thursday, at a Rosh Hashanah toast at the Defense Ministry, Katz said: “There are signs we are seeing that indicate that the severe economic pressure Iran is under and fears of an uprising and the fall of the regime could push them toward desperate steps.” He went on to warn that an Iranian attack on Israel would “release us from all constraints” and lead Israel to strike “all infrastructure, including energy infrastructure.” However, a source familiar with the issue said that “Katz wants to remain relevant and make headlines.” At the same time, officials stressed that there was no special military preparation underway. That does not mean Israel is failing to prepare for the possibility of escalation. Defensive preparations are ongoing at all times, including for a range of scenarios in which Iran attacks Israel, but there is no assessment that such an attack is imminent. On the contrary, Israeli officials believe Iran has no real interest in drawing Israel into the fighting. Trump also does not want Israel involved, they say, to avoid turning the confrontation into a wider regional conflict. Speaking at the toast at the Kirya military headquarters in Tel Aviv, Netanyahu said the Iranian regime “is faltering. It is weaker than ever. It is fighting for its survival.” “I am confident in our ability to remove this threat once and for all. In other words, to topple this regime,” he said. “That is the central mission that still lies ahead of us, but it is close. It is not impossible. It is within reach.” “They are not avoiding attacking us by accident,” Netanyahu continued. “They are attacking everyone except us. They know our strength, the force of our blows and our determination. I say to our enemies: Don’t mess with us.” In any case, the Jewish holiday period is always considered particularly sensitive in Israel, and Katz therefore felt a need to strengthen deterrence against Iran to prevent Tehran from being tempted to attack. At the same time, the professional assessment within the IDF and the defense establishment is that Iran has no concrete intention of acting against Israel, and there has been no change in the military’s level of preparedness. Meanwhile, U.S. Vice President JD Vance again blamed Europe on Thursday for high fuel prices, saying the increase was being driven by Iranian attacks on commercial shipping. He argued that the situation underscored what he described as the decline of Washington’s European allies and their inability to do more to help maintain a steady supply of energy to global markets. Vance questioned why the United States should be the only country capable of ensuring that global energy markets remain adequately supplied. Despite exchanges of fire this week between the United States and Iran, Vance said he would not characterize the situation as a war, noting that there was no active shooting at the time. He said the United States was using a range of measures to pressure Iran to stop targeting commercial shipping, while acknowledging that Tehran was still likely to continue such attacks. Vance added that Washington had many additional tools available, some of which President Donald Trump might use and others he might not. He said all options remained under consideration, including economic, military, diplomatic and covert pressure. He also rejected the suggestion that the United States was doing too little against Iran, arguing that the alternative would be far more costly. According to Vance, Gulf Arab states had urged Washington not to pursue that alternative, as had several other countries, including European nations. Vance said the U.S. message to Iran had remained unchanged from the outset: Tehran must stop firing on commercial shipping. On negotiations, he said Trump had made clear that the United States was not in talks with Iran and would not enter talks unless Iran stopped attacking commercial vessels.
news.summary: Iran threatened a 'powerful response' to a full-scale strike on Ali Taher, but Israeli officials said they see no sign of imminent action; Netanyahu said regime change is 'within reach'; Vance ruled out talks unless Iran stops firing
news.author: Itamar Eichner, Daniel Edelson, New York

news.title: Tesla rolls out steering-wheel-free Cybercabs in Austin
news.text:
Elon Musk sent dozens of self-driving Cybercabs without steering wheels or brake pedals onto the streets of Austin, Texas, on Thursday, betting that Americans will overcome their fears of rides with “no control” and hop inside.

The rollout of the gold-coloured Teslas, which give passengers no way to take control in an emergency, comes as the company prepares to launch the service in other cities.

Tesla shares have suffered amid a slump in vehicle sales, but they rose more than 5 per cent Thursday on hopes that the futuristic-looking taxis will catch on quickly.

“No steering wheel, no pedals,” Tesla teased on X before the launch. Musk followed with a post showing a giant Cybercab floating above the Austin skyline and later wrote, “A Storm of Cybercabs.” An invitation-only launch event was expected to be held later Thursday.

Tesla faces a race to catch Waymo

It is unclear how soon Musk intends to roll out the Cybercab service, but he needs to move quickly.

Tesla trails self-driving taxi leader Waymo in the number of cabs deployed and trips completed. To catch up, it must demonstrate that its camera-only system can safely navigate streets and avoid pedestrians. By contrast, Waymo and another rival, Amazon’s Zoox, supplement cameras with radar and a laser-based technology called lidar.

Americans remain wary of driverless cars

Even if the technology works well, Americans still need to be convinced.

A Pew Research Center survey conducted in February found that seven in 10 US adults were “not too” or “not at all” comfortable riding in a driverless car.

Tesla stock was battered last year after Musk took over President Donald Trump’s government cost-cutting campaign, dubbed DOGE, and embraced extreme-right political candidates, sparking protests at Tesla showrooms and boycotts by car buyers in several countries.

Tesla posted a second consecutive annual decline in vehicle sales last year. Its profits plunged, and it lost its crown as the world’s best-selling electric vehicle maker to China’s BYD.

Austin already has Tesla robotaxis

Austin has had a self-driving Tesla “robotaxi” service since June last year, but those cars are equipped with steering wheels and brake pedals. The service, which has since expanded to five other cities in Texas and Florida, initially carried passengers with safety drivers aboard to take over in case of problems.

Tesla has more than 200 “unsupervised” robotaxis in those cities, meaning they operate without safety drivers aboard, according to the monitoring site RobotaxiTracker. Waymo has more than 4,000 such vehicles in 14 cities.

In the Pew survey, 16 per cent of US adults said they would be “somewhat” comfortable riding in a driverless car, while 7 per cent said they would be “extremely” or “very” comfortable.

Separate Gallup polling conducted in 2025 found that skepticism about the safety of driverless cars had risen over the previous several years. More Americans said all or mostly human-operated cars were the safest option than in a 2018 poll.

Musk faces his own trust challenge

It is unclear whether Musk is the right person to coax people into cars with no human controls. Another Pew poll conducted in January found that nearly six in 10 US adults had a “very” or “mostly” unfavourable view of him.

Musk eventually hopes to send full self-driving software to hundreds of thousands of Teslas through a software update. That would allow Tesla owners to turn their cars into taxis for hire when they are not using them.

Regulatory scrutiny adds to Tesla’s challenges

But regulators in the US and overseas have signalled that he still has some convincing to do.

Tesla has not received approval for drivers to use even its partial self-driving software in most European Union countries. In the US, where the software has been downloaded and used, regulators have opened several investigations into its safety.

One probe is examining the software’s role in several Tesla crashes in fog, sun glare and other low-visibility conditions, including one in which a pedestrian was killed.

Another is investigating dozens of incidents in which Teslas using partial self-driving software ran red lights or drove on the wrong side of the road, sometimes crashing into other vehicles and causing injuries. A third is examining why Tesla apparently violated regulatory requirements by failing to report crashes promptly.

Published on September 4, 2026
news.summary: The rollout comes as Tesla seeks to prove its camera-only system can safely navigate streets while winning over sceptical American passengers

news.title: US tariff probe into Southeast Asia raises kosher food supply concerns
news.text:
Fatty acids from palm and other vegetable oils are used in a range of kosher products including mayonnaise, margarine and other processed foods. (EPA Images pic)
WASHINGTON: A tariff investigation in president Donald Trump’s administration has spurred an unlikely critic: one of the largest Orthodox Jewish groups in the US.
The Orthodox Union, which calls itself the biggest kosher certification agency in the world, warned commerce secretary Howard Lutnick in a letter that tariffs on vegetable-based fatty acids would threaten the supply chain for kosher foods. Fatty acids from palm and other vegetable oils are used in a range of products including margarine, mayonnaise and other processed foods.
The opposition is an example of how the tariffs have shaken up global supply chains in novel ways. The Orthodox Union argued that the proposed duties could increase costs for kosher foods without creating additional domestic supply because alternative animal-based oils and fatty acids are largely not considered kosher.
“To me, the big deal here, is that we’re speaking about a fundamental, basic food ingredient,” said Rabbi Moshe Elefant, chief executive officer of OU Kosher. “It’s not like saying, ‘don’t eat something fancy if you can’t afford it.’”
“This is something that’s found in everything,” he said.
A plurality of voters are concerned about the cost of living with the approach of the midterm elections, according to pollsters. Seventy-one percent of registered voters disapproved of how Trump is handling the issue in an Aug 31 survey conducted by Reuters and Ipsos.
The commerce department is investigating whether some vegetable-based fatty acids from Indonesia and Malaysia are unfairly burdening the domestic market.
A preliminary determination found that at least some tariffs were justified, and the agency proposed a countervailing duty of about 16.5% on vegetable-based fatty acids from Indonesia. Most of those products that originate in Malaysia will be subject to a duty of at least 4%. Final tariff rates are expected by the end of the year.
The inquiry was prompted by petition by Chicago-based Vantage Specialty Chemicals, which also produces vegetable-based fatty acids. The company argued in January that fatty acid imports were harming US manufacturing.
“Dumping of foreign government-subsidised fatty acids has significantly damaged competitiveness and is undermining American manufacturing,” Mike Waldron, a senior vice-president of corporate affairs, said in a January statement.
The commerce department and Vantage Specialty Chemicals didn’t respond to a request for comment.
news.summary: A kosher certification agency warns that tariffs on vegetable-based fatty acids from Malaysia and Indonesia threaten the kosher food supply chain.
news.author: Bloomberg

news.title: All Options Against Iran "On Table", Including Covert Pressure: JD Vance
news.text: US Vice President JD Vance on Thursday (local time) said that the Trump administration has a range of options at its disposal to deal with Iran, including economic, military, diplomatic and covert measures, as tensions between Washington and Tehran continue to escalate amid the conflict in West Asia.Speaking during a media briefing, Vance said the administration would not publicly disclose its plans for engaging with Iran, stressing that doing so would limit US President Donald Trump's ability to make decisions."There are a lot of additional tools that we have at our disposal. Some of those the President will use and some of them he won't," Vance said."But everything that could happen is on the table. Economic pressure, military pressure, diplomatic pressure, covert pressure. Of course these are tools in the President's toolkit," he added.Vance said the administration's approach was also aimed at preventing a wider global energy crisis, accusing Iran of continuing to target commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz."We would have had an energy crisis because the Iranians refuse to stop acting like terrorists in the Strait of Hormuz," Vance said, while defending the US military's efforts to protect commercial shipping and maintain the flow of oil and gas.The Vice President said Washington had to retain flexibility in deciding how to respond to Tehran and declined to spell out what measures could be adopted in the coming months."Part of the reason they're tools in the toolkit is because the Vice President, hopefully, is not dumb enough to stand up before all of you and a million Americans watching at home and say exactly what it is that we plan on doing," Vance said.His remarks come as the seven-month-old conflict between the US and Iran shows few signs of a lasting resolution, despite indications that Trump may be considering declaring the war over.According to a Wall Street Journal report, Trump is privately weighing whether to declare an end to the war, particularly as the US approaches midterm elections and energy prices remain elevated because of the conflict. At the same time, the Pentagon has extended troop deployments in West Asia, raising the possibility that military tensions could persist into next year.The report came amid a fresh wave of strikes between the two sides. The United States Central Command said it had conducted strikes against multiple sites inside Iran, while Tehran responded with attacks on US-linked facilities across the Gulf.Trump, meanwhile, said on Wednesday that he did not expect the conflict, which began on February 28, to continue for "very much longer".Speaking to reporters at the Oval Office, Trump said US forces had carried out a "very heavy attack" on Iran the previous night, targeting newly established military equipment along the Strait of Hormuz, including radar and missile-related systems."We hit them hard last night, very hard. They gave a little love tap, but we hit them very hard last night," Trump said.The escalation comes shortly after the Trump administration launched "Operation Economic Outcast", a campaign announced by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to intensify economic pressure on Iran.The operation is aimed at targeting what Washington describes as Tehran's principal economic lifelines, including oil, shipping, aviation and digital assets. Bessent said the campaign seeks to cut Iran off from international financial networks and restrict revenue streams supporting the Iranian government. news.title: Social media: Can Meta’s billions replace parenting?
news.text:
Recently, the American company Meta, owner of Facebook, agreed to pay $18bn for social media content that allegedly harms kids. The amount is for an out-of-court settlement in one court case, and as everyone cites it as reason to threaten more lawsuits against Meta, it makes one ponder. This is more so as no one talks about what common sense demands where raising kids is in focus. No one mentions the place of effective parenting and I find it alarming, to put it mildly. It seems there’s this self- censorship to not mention the role of parents among people who discuss social media impacts on kids. Yet, I think emphasising parenting should be the first and more effective approach, even as Meta tidies up its end to any extent it can. Discussions in public spaces make it seem like parents should be responsible for everything about their kids except the digital devices they place in the hands of kids. Where blood, bond, and love play a part, I don’t think any external entities can take on the role of a parent and do it better than the parent.

On TV shows, anchors and guests avoid talking about the role of parents in guiding their kids in this matter. They quickly drop it and move away as though it’s a hot plate whenever anyone mentions parents, a phenomenon I think is deliberate and hypocritical. What some want to hear is what contributors are saying regarding parents, kids, and the effects of social media on them. Mentioning the positive impact on kids of a parent’s firm “No” has suddenly become a taboo. Does a medical doctor avoid talking about what a sick patient needs to hear in order for them to heal? What should be common sense in this social media challenge is being sidestepped. Who should regulate access to digital devices in the home? Government? Owners of social media platforms that aren’t in the home? There are workers on those platforms who, knowing the effects, guide their own kids appropriately just like makers of some processed foods neither eat them nor give their kids. As for a section of the public, their parental responsibilities belong to someone else. I belong to the Yoruba tribe in Nigeria that places great emphasis on how parents raise their kids. Effective parenting is one way we pass on our values to kids, and many other Nigerian tribes testify to the outcome they see.

Regarding how a kid behaves, the Yoruba descend first on parents before they ask any outsiders. When a kid misbehaves, the Yoruba don’t blame the kid; they send strong messages to the parents. Many of our proverbs and wise sayings capture this, and they guide a parent’s sense of parenting. The Yoruba don’t lease out parenting. We see danger, and we keep our kids away from it. So, it should baffle a Yoruba person what we see in our world these days. I take note of the age of some of the kids reported to have become victims of harmful online materials. Some are seven or eight years old. Without meaning to justify harmful content on social media, there’s a question I’ve always asked: What is a digital device that can access harmful social media content doing in the hands of a seven-year-old kid who should still be blissfully living in the wonderful innocence of a seven-year-old? Watch all the TV shows; no one asks this question. No contributor mentions it.

Another intriguing thing is the economic class of many of the people who’re reported to have been affected by social media content such that they commit suicide. This has made me ponder, for example, that President Donald Trump’s rich parents obviously didn’t let him have access to things that damaged many young people of his generation. The US president is so physically healthy at 80 that it’s unbelievable. His doctors publicly marveled at this fact. Obviously, Trump didn’t abuse what many in his younger days did despite the fact that he was raised in a rich home. His parents guided him properly. Perhaps the Yoruba DNA in her was speaking out when Kemi Badenoch, Conservative Party leader in the UK, said recently, “We don’t allow children to go to nightclubs, so why do we allow them in spaces that are not good for them?” Badenoch, of Nigerian ancestry, was talking about the need for parents to monitor their kids regarding social media.

I suppose it’s the centrality of parental control over kids that makes some satellite TV companies list steps parents can take to keep kids away from TV channels with adult-specific content. It’s for the same reason movies are labeled according to the age category that should watch them. In Nigeria, it’s a lot of conversations about either getting or not getting mobile phones in homes where parents make kids receive calls from friends on their phones. Except for some rich homes, most parents are wary of giving a smart phone with access to social media to a child under 16. Parents here get their kids engaged in some other activities rather than watch them spend hours on smartphones. What obtains in other climes? Seven-year-old kids are given mobile phones, which by the age of fifteen are said to have damaged their emotional well-being to the extent that they commit suicide. 

I think if kids could be protected from alcohol, tobacco, hard drugs, etc., they should be protected from digital devices that give them access to content that can damage their minds. This is first a parent’s duty before it’s the government’s. Nigerians have a saying about the person who spends their money to purchase what can harm them. But what can the government do in this matter? Get social media platforms to limit harmful content. Governments are doing this, yet the problem doesn’t go away. It won’t, because a problem that requires a multi-pronged approach to solve is now projected as having only one solution. It’s what the current determination to file more suits against Meta indicates. The matter is made worse as owners of social media platforms don’t admit any wrongdoing.

Meta, for instance, doesn’t believe its content harms kids; it doesn’t believe it’s the single factor that harms kids.

There’s also a mentality I observe among producers of items that allegedly cause harm. Their body language is like, “We want you to take our product, but we don’t expect that you won’t take it in moderation; we presume you know what’s good for you.” There was once a controversy over pasta made by a company in Nigeria. Those who know say the company uses lead as a preservative. The company responds by saying lead in their product is added at the rate nutritionists say is not harmful to health. That tells me something straightaway: There’s a limited portion an individual should eat each day; eat more than the kilogram needed and health problems may arise. Lead can accumulate in the body and affect health, so, as far as the company is concerned, consumers who make a habit of eating too much of this pasta daily do so at their own risk. Clearly, the makers of any product want to make money, and they’ll do everything to get as many people as possible hooked.

I observe also that governments can’t fully restrain the billion-dollar companies. For example, the best that governments do to the alcohol and tobacco industry is ensure their products aren’t sold to kids. Governments don’t stop them from producing what they do. Governments won’t stop them because they need taxes from these large companies, and when they don’t get enough, they can’t provide the public services citizens want to see before they vote for politicians. Such web is default – political and economic system – skewed against the parent that’s lax in guiding their kids. The political and economic interests of politicians and companies make them less inclined towards taking on a responsibility they privately believe should be for parents. Those comments by political leaders about putting more noose on companies over their social media content are more for political correctness, not exactly what they believe. It means confronting this problem solely by constantly slamming Meta with lawsuits will be a vicious cycle, and billion-dollar companies will play along for as long as they continue to make money.

Meanwhile, some nations have banned access to social media for kids below 16. I think this will allow kids to be kids. For anyone below 16, a laptop or palmtop is okay for them to do their academic work and have some form of digital fun, including video games. While some governments restrict kids’ access to social media, others vow to continue to sue Meta and get payments for harms done to kids. As public commentators in some climes shy away from asking parents to watch the kind of digital devices they place in the hands of their kids, I ask: Can the billions of dollars Meta is compelled to pay in court ever be a substitute for parenting?
news.summary:
Explore the debate on social media’s impact on kids and the overlooked role of effective parenting. Can Meta’s settlements replace parental guidance?

news.title: China responded to some of US requests regarding ‘economic war on Iran’ — Vance
news.text:
WASHINGTON, September 4. /TASS/. Chinese authorities have responded to a number of requests regarding Washington’s recently declared ‘economic war’ on Iran, US Vice President JD Vance has told reporters.

When asked whether US President Donald Trump directly asked Chinese President Xi Jinping to bar Chinese banks from offering financial services to Iran, Vance replied: "We've certainly had a number of conversations with the Chinese, and frankly, I think the Chinese have been responsive to some of the requests that we've made. I actually don't know whether the president has spoken directly to [President] Xi, but we will get an answer for you and follow up."

Speaking about isolation of Iran, Vance said that, in his opinion, China is "willing to play ball here, and we all know this."

"They are, in that way, I think, willing to be a little bit more responsible. Again, I'm not saying they're doing everything that we've asked them to do, but I think that the PRC has been much more responsible, certainly than the Iranians, and much more responsible than a couple of other nations as well," the US vice president continued.

"But it's not just the PRC. If you look at Turkey, if you look at Azerbaijan, if you look at UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, a lot of the Gulf Arab coalition. If you look all across the world, we're actually seeing a lot of countries. Sometimes they're not willing to say so publicly, but privately they're doing a lot of good things to help us ensure that the Iranians pay a penalty for firing at commercial shipping," he said.

Chinese Ministry of Commerce Spokesperson Huang Ling said on Thursday the Chinese government will resist US sanctions for trade with Iran. She reiterated Beijing’s "strong dissatisfaction and firm opposition" to unilateral sanctions that are not authorized by the UN Security Council and have no basis in international law.
news.summary: Speaking about isolation of Iran, the US vice president said that, in his opinion, China is "willing to play ball here, and we all know this"

news.text: South Korea is preparing to deploy military assets to support freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and aims to dispatch them before the end of the year, media reported late on Thursday, citing government and military sources.The reports in several South Korean media outlets said the government was preparing procedures to seek parliamentary approval for the deployment, including submitting a consent motion to parliament this month after cabinet review.The government was considering options including sending a maritime patrol aircraft, a logistics support vessel or a mine detection and clearance unit, and had been discussing the scale and nature of a potential contribution with countries including the United States, Britain and France, the reports said. news.title: JD Vance takes ruthless swipe at Joe Biden’s health in first White House briefing since Karoline Leavitt exit
news.text:
Vice President JD Vance has taken a cutting swipe at former President Joe Biden’s cognitive fitness, delivering a sarcastic jab during his first White House press briefing since Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt stepped down.

Taking the podium in the James S. Brady Press Briefing Room on Thursday afternoon—the White House's first formal media briefing in over 40 days—Vance fielded questions on inflation, foreign policy, and upcoming memorial plans.

The conversation quickly turned to next week’s 25th anniversary commemorations of the September 11 terrorist attacks, where living former commanders-in-chief are expected to assemble at Ground Zero in New York City.

With President Donald Trump scheduled to mark the anniversary at the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, Vance confirmed that he would represent the administration in Manhattan alongside former presidents Barack Obama, Bill Clinton, George W. Bush, and Joe Biden.

Asked about crossing paths with the 83-year-old former president, Vance couldn't resist a sarcastic dig aimed directly at Biden's mental sharpness.

"As you guys can probably guess, I'm really looking forward to hanging out with Joe Biden," Vance told reporters with a grin. "I'm sure that we'll have many, many intense intellectual conversations, and, you know, it'll be great. We'll have a great time with Joe Biden and the other presidents."

The cutting remark drew immediate reactions in the room, referencing the long-running conservative criticism regarding Biden's age, cognitive health, and public speaking stumbles that ultimately led to his withdrawal from the 2024 presidential race.

Vance brushed aside speculation that Trump's absence from the Ground Zero ceremony was due to security considerations or disputes over speaking roles, insisting the decision was purely logistical.

"We'd like to be three or four places on 9/11, but you can't have one person be in multiple locations at the exact same time," Vance explained. "We just decided as a team that I would go to New York for 9/11, [and] the president would stay in D.C., of course, to commemorate what happened at the Pentagon, because that was a critical part of the tragedy of 9/11 as well."

The briefing marked Vance’s first appearance behind the podium since Karoline Leavitt officially concluded her historic tenure as White House Press Secretary late last month. Leavitt, who left the post to transition to a senior role at the pro-Trump super PAC MAGA Inc., has yet to be formally replaced, leaving senior administration figures like Vance to handle press room inquiries.

Despite the political barb, Vance struck a more reflective tone regarding the solemnity of the upcoming anniversary, urging younger Americans who were not alive during the 2001 attacks to tune in.

"I think that sense of commonality and common purpose that we all had on 9/11, that's something that we should really try every single day to get back to," Vance added. "If even just for a day, even if just for a few hours, I would encourage people to tune in."
news.summary: The Vice President sarcastically claimed he is looking forward to "many intense intellectual conversations" with the former president

news.title: Met chief is stunned by the release of serial criminals: Scotland Yard boss 'is flabbergasted' serious knife and firearm offenders are bailed 'again and again'
news.text:
Violent criminals are being freed on bail to commit murder amid the prison overcrowding crisis, the country's top police officer warned.

Met Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley said he was 'flabbergasted' at the growing number of suspects charged with gun and knife crimes who are being let back on to the streets.

Sir Mark said he expected to see a rise in violent crime, with some offenders still being freed on bail on their fourth offence of being caught with a weapon.

In explosive testimony to the London Policing Board, the Scotland Yard chief revealed that more than 30 people charged with serious firearms offences in London alone were currently on bail.

And the Mail can reveal that there are now a staggering 3,000 electronic tag breaches by bailed suspects every week across England and Wales.

 In nine out of ten cases, the courts re-release them on bail, which will embolden serial offenders, police chiefs fear.

Victims' advocates said the creaking criminal justice system was now creating serious implications for public safety.

It comes as thousands of criminals are set to be let out early under Labour's controversial Sentencing Act aimed at tackling overcrowding.

Sir Mark said: 'This isn't a theoretical risk. We are seeing stabbings and in one or two cases homicides committed by people who would previously have been on remand in custody. This is really troubling.'

In the last six months alone, the number of bailed suspects breaching their electronic tag conditions has rocketed by nearly 50 per cent in London alone, from 2,977 in January to 4,408 in July.

Breaches can include going on the run, contacting a victim, flouting a curfew, attempting to remove a tag or going to a prohibited area.

The Met Commissioner added: 'In more than 95 per cent of those cases we arrest them, put them before the courts and nothing changes, so that looks like nugatory [futile] effort.'

In some instances, those released on bail are going on to carry out murders. 

Sir Mark warned falls in knife crime were 'starting to turn' as a result of 'compromised' offender control, adding: 'I'm really worried about that.

'We are seeing rapidly reducing imprisonment for people sentenced for knife crime offences, even repeat knife carriers.

'At the start of the process far fewer are being remanded in custody, so routinely now we are seeing people charged again, and again, and again with carrying knives and they are being bailed again, and again, and again, and that really concerns me.' 

At the weekend, a repeat knife offender on bail was caught trying to smuggle an 18-inch sword into the Notting Hill Carnival in his fourth blade offence that year.

Sir Mark said: 'He is on bail and has two knife referral orders and tries to take something that looks like a small sword into Notting Hill Carnival and he is bailed again. 

'That is deeply concerning to me – the message that sends and that fundamentally undermines offender control. We are now seeing it on firearms offences as well and I'm flabbergasted by this.

'There are 34 cases of people being charged with firearms offences in London pending trial who are on bail, in nine of those cases they have fired shots in confrontations and they are on bail.'

Police chiefs fear Labour's soft justice reforms will make matters worse as short sentences are ditched, meaning fewer offenders will be jailed, and police will have to monitor thousands of criminals released early.

Jason Hogg, Chief Constable of Thames Valley Police, agreed that soft-touch bail conditions were a symptom of a 'criminal justice system in crisis'. 

He said: 'Already the whole Sentencing Act hasn't properly kicked in and I'm receiving reports it's more difficult to remand people to custody. 

'We have about 4,000 breaches of court bail each week. And in over 90 per cent of those, the conditions aren't changed.'

The warning comes after a series of cases where suspects freed on bail have gone on to commit murders.

Victims' Commissioner Claire Waxman said: 'What started as a prison capacity crisis has evolved into a whole-system challenge for criminal justice, with implications for public safety, victim confidence and the effective operation of prisons, probation, policing, courts and victim services.'

A government spokesman said that since Labour took office 'knife crime has fallen by 11 per cent and knife homicides by 26 per cent'. 

The spokesman added: 'Bail decisions are a matter for the independent judiciary.'

On Thursday, Donald Trump repeated claims that parts of London were no-go areas as a result of immigration. 

The President also used the GB News interview to renew criticism of London Mayor, Lord Khan of Tooting.

Mr Trump said: 'London's a much different place. You have a terrible mayor. He's a nasty guy, nasty person.

'You have areas in Paris and London where the police don't want to go in them, there's no law and order. They're afraid to go in them.'

But a source close to Lord Khan said: 'Sadiq is still living rent free in Trump's head. The guy is obsessed with him.
news.summary: Met Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley said he was 'flabbergasted' at the growing number of suspects charged with gun and knife crimes who are being let back on to the streets.

news.title: Cut petroleum product imports, CORAN urges govt
news.text:
The Crude Oil Refinery Owners Association of Nigeria has urged the Federal Government to urgently strengthen the domestic refining industry and reduce the country’s dependence on imported petroleum products.

The association made the call in a position paper titled “Position Paper on the Urgent Need for Strategic Government Intervention to Strengthen Nigeria’s Domestic Refining Industry,” while citing the recent intervention by United States President Donald Trump in the American refining sector as a lesson for Nigeria.

It argued that Nigeria had an even stronger case for government intervention because local refinery operators faced foreign-exchange pressures, high borrowing costs, limited access to long-tenor financing, crude supply challenges, inadequate infrastructure, and high logistics costs.

“It is sound industrial policy. It is an energy-security policy. And ultimately, it is economic policy,” the association stated.

The group expressed concern that Nigeria, despite being one of Africa’s largest crude oil producers, continued to experience difficulties in supplying crude to domestic refineries on commercially workable terms.

It said that during the first quarter of 2026, 61.9 million barrels were allocated to domestic refineries while producers offered 68.7 million barrels, but only 28.5 million barrels were actually delivered.

According to the association, the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission identified pricing gaps between producers and domestic refiners as one of the major reasons crude offered did not translate into completed transactions.

It, however, acknowledged improvements in the second quarter, saying NUPRC reported that 53.7 million barrels of crude oil and condensate were supplied to local refineries, representing reported Domestic Crude Supply Obligation performance of 97.4 per cent.

“CORAN acknowledges and commends this improvement,” it stated. The association, however, stressed that crude allocation alone was insufficient, noting that refineries required crude delivered under commercially sustainable conditions.

“A refinery does not consume an allocation on paper. It consumes crude delivered under commercially sustainable terms,” CORAN stated. It called for greater consideration of pricing, transportation, evacuation infrastructure, crude quality, financing, payment arrangements and proximity to producing assets when determining crude supply arrangements.

The refinery owners also called for a commercially sensible pricing template for crude supplied to domestic refineries. They acknowledged that international benchmarks such as Brent, WTI and Platts were useful market references but argued that they should not be applied mechanically where refiners were also required to bear separate evacuation and logistics costs.

The association proposed a Domestic Refinery Crude Pricing Framework that would consider internationally recognised crude benchmark values, quality differentials, the actual point of delivery, avoided international freight and insurance costs, domestic evacuation and logistics costs, proximity between producing fields and refineries, as well as reasonable commercial margins for producers.

“The objective is not subsidised crude. The objective is correctly priced crude,” CORAN stated. The refinery owners also expressed concern over the resurgence of petroleum-product imports, urging the government to ensure imports increasingly serve only as a mechanism for addressing supply gaps.

They cited NMDPRA data showing that domestic PMS supply fell from approximately 32.5 million litres per day in June 2026 to 25.8 million litres per day in July, while petrol imports rose from about 18.1 million litres to 19.7 million litres per day.

The association said Nigeria needed adequate petroleum-product stocks and was not advocating policies that could create artificial shortages. However, it warned that a continuous import regime alongside growing domestic refining investment could weaken incentives for existing and prospective refineries.

“A continuous import regime existing alongside substantial domestic refining investment exports Nigerian jobs and refining margins, places additional demand on foreign exchange, weakens investment incentives for existing and prospective refineries, exposes Nigeria to international freight disruptions and geopolitical shocks, and ultimately undermines the country’s aspiration to become a petroleum-product refining and export hub,” it stated.

The group called for import licences to increasingly be calibrated against independently verified domestic production and supply gaps. It added that domestic production capable of meeting equivalent specifications and commercial requirements should receive priority in the Nigerian market.

The association identified access to finance as one of the biggest constraints facing Nigeria’s emerging refining industry. It said refineries were capital-intensive projects requiring substantial investment in processing units, storage facilities, utilities, pipelines, loading facilities, environmental infrastructure, laboratories, fire-protection systems and working capital.

It further urged the government to treat refineries as industrial infrastructure rather than merely downstream petroleum businesses. “Every barrel refined within Nigeria has the potential to retain economic value that would otherwise leave the country,” it stated.

According to the association, domestic refining supports employment, engineering services, fabrication, transportation, petrochemicals, lubricants, plastics, construction materials and other industries while conserving foreign exchange.

It called for a network of large, medium-sized and modular refineries strategically distributed around producing basins and major consumption centres. “The success of one refinery should not mark the completion of Nigeria’s refining ambition. Nigeria requires an ecosystem,” CORAN stated.

To address the challenges, CORAN called on the Federal Government to convene an urgent Presidential Refining Industry Roundtable involving the association, NUPRC, NMDPRA, NNPC Limited, crude producers, financial institutions, infrastructure investors and relevant government ministries.

The association proposed 10 priority actions, including the full institutionalisation of naira-for-crude, development of a domestic crude pricing template, stronger enforcement of the Domestic Crude Supply Obligation under Section 109 of the Petroleum Industry Act and increased use of crude swaps.

It also called for the progressive reduction of petroleum-product imports, creation of a refinery development financing framework, development of shared petroleum-product infrastructure and establishment of strategic petroleum-product reserves.

The group further proposed regulatory and fiscal incentives for refinery expansion, particularly investments in conversion units capable of increasing domestic production of PMS, AGO, aviation fuel and LPG.

“Government intervention should therefore increasingly move away from subsidising consumption and toward enabling production,” it stated. The association added, “Support the refinery. Support the pipeline. Support the storage terminal. Support access to commercially priced Nigerian crude. Support long-term industrial finance.”

CORAN said Nigeria should ultimately become a refining hub for Africa. “Nigeria should not continue exporting crude, exporting jobs and importing the same petroleum products at considerable economic cost.

“Our crude must increasingly power our refineries. Our refineries must increasingly supply our market. And Nigeria must ultimately become a refining hub for Africa. That should be the destination of petroleum-sector reform,” the association stated.

news.title: Trump Admin Asks Supreme Court to Restore Mail-Ballot Rules Before Midterms
news.text:
The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court on Thursday to allow restrictions on mail-in ballots in an attempt to prevent illegal aliens from voting in the November midterm elections.

news.title: South Korea prepares to deploy troops to Strait of Hormuz
news.text:
South Korea is preparing to deploy troops to the Strait of Hormuz as part of an international force aimed at keeping the strait open for maritime traffic, according to South Korean media.

The South Korean government is preparing to submit a motion to the National Assembly for consent to move troops out of Korea.

The government told JTBC News that they were "reviewing deployment plans" with the goal of stabilizing the Strait of Hormuz and protecting South Korean shipping. The government said it expects the motion to pass quickly.

However, even if the bill moves rapidly through the Korean parliament, the final vote is expected to align with South Korean President Lee Jae-myung's anticipated visit to the UN General Assembly between September 18-28, according to the Korean East Asia Daily (Dong-A Ilbo).

Despite the resolve to deploy, the South Korean government has not yet decided on the specifics of the deployment, including assets and personnel. 

South Korea's anti-piracy naval force is already in the Gulf of Aden to ward off Somali pirates and has been deployed to the region since 2009.

US President Donald Trump requested that South Korea send warships to the Strait of Hormuz as early as March. Prior to the closure of the strait, South Korea purchased approximately 70% of its oil from the Middle East.

This move comes despite a deterioration in relations between Israel and South Korea, following President Lee's condemnation of the detention of Gaza Freedom Flotilla activists, including prominent South Korean activist Kim Ah-hyun. 

President Lee also received strong condemnation from Israel's Foreign Ministry in April after sharing a video claiming to show Israeli troops torturing and murdering a Palestinian child, saying that what the IDF was doing was "no different from the Jewish massacre" by the Nazis. His remarks came on the eve of Holocaust Remembrance Day.
